committee: CC Commission for Persons with Disabilities
overview: The CC Commission for Persons with Disabilities advocates for the equal status of residents with disabilities by monitoring ADA compliance in Medford’s municipal infrastructure, programs, and services. Since 2023, the body has focused on removing physical barriers at public schools, City Hall, and transit stations while organizing annual community resource fairs. The commission maintains a digital repository of accessibility resources and provides input on inclusive designs for city playgrounds and polling places. As of late 2026, the body is collaborating with the Institute for Human Centered Design on a city-wide accessibility transition plan and prioritizing intersections for the installation of accessible pedestrian signals.

threads.name: Disability Pride and Resource Fair
threads.summary: The commission coordinates an annual event featuring resource vendors, speakers, and inclusive activities like sensory quiet spaces [M01#4, M15#2]. Planning began in early 2023 for a spring event, which was eventually held in October 2023 with a focus on vaccinations and vendor networking [M03#2, M08#3]. Subsequent fairs were held or planned for May 2025 and May 2026, including features such as inclusive dance performances and mayoral proclamations [M14#8, M17#4, M18#4]. By late 2026, the commission began discussing schedule adjustments to move future fairs to the autumn [M19#2].

threads.name: Public Transit Advocacy
threads.summary: The body advocates for accessibility improvements at key transit hubs, including the West Medford commuter rail station and the Tufts Green Line Extension (GLX) station [M03#6, M07#6]. Early efforts focused on supporting funding for West Medford and securing accessible parking at the new Tufts station, which was resolved with two painted spots in late 2023 [M08#5, M14#4]. The commission also monitors 'The Ride' paratransit services and reviews proposed MBTA bus route changes presented by Director of Traffic and Transportation Todd Blake [M02#6, M15#4, M19#4].

threads.name: Municipal Building and Park Accessibility
threads.summary: The commission reviews ADA compliance across city facilities, from physical barriers at Medford High School to hearing accessibility upgrades in the City Hall chambers [M01#4, M14#3, M15#3]. Members provide feedback on inclusive playground designs, including projects at Carr Park and the Tufts Park redesign [M04#4, M08#6, M18#2]. Recently, the Institute for Human Centered Design (IHCD) completed accessibility surveys of municipal structures and sidewalks to inform a city-wide transition plan [M19#3, M20#2].

threads.name: Digital Resources and Website Management
threads.summary: The commission maintains a dedicated section on the city website to provide vetted accessibility and recreational resources for residents [M01#2]. Members identified errors and missing transportation data during a site transition in 2023 and subsequently audited the page to include accordions for various services [M02#3, M12#7]. Collaborative efforts with the Medford Senior Center and the Medford Public Library have expanded the site's listings for tax assistance and adaptive technology [M10#3, M10#6]. Recent work involves monitoring the city's progress toward full digital accessibility compliance [M17#6].

threads.name: Voting and Polling Place Readiness
threads.summary: The commission focuses on the accessibility of the political sphere by verifying that polling locations are prepared for voters with disabilities [M13#5]. Members coordinate with the Elections Commission to ensure accessible voting machines are properly set up, calibrated, and staffed by trained workers [M13#4, M16#9]. Recent efforts include reviewing voting machine accessibility testing results and discussing alternative voting methods [M18#7].

threads.name: Commission Identity and Governance
threads.summary: The commission has periodically reviewed the city ordinance governing its powers to ensure its role in advocating for residents remains current [M04#5, M13#5]. Governance activities have included electing officers like Gabrielle Evangelista as secretary and naming Gabby as interim chair following the departure of Tom Hamel [M01#5, M08#8]. Members also explored a formal name change and rebranding through a new logo designed in collaboration with local students [M01#3, M07#8, M08#4]. In 2026, staff reported that an updated commission ordinance was undergoing legal review [M18#6].

threads.name: Pedestrian Infrastructure and Signals
threads.summary: The commission prioritizes the installation of ADA-compliant audible pedestrian signals at intersections throughout the city [M20#3]. In 2026, Director of Traffic and Transportation Todd Blake detailed plans for upgrades at multiple intersections funded by a casino mitigation grant [M19#4]. This work coincides with discussions regarding sidewalk conditions, snow removal requirements, and the importance of planting accessible tree species that do not damage walkways [M14#9, M15#4, M17#7].
